html:
José Matías Delgado was a Salvadoran priest who led the first call for independence in Central America, in San Salvador on 5 November 1811. He is called the Father of the Nation.

Merchants and creoles of San Salvador resented the control of Guatemala City over the indigo trade. In 1811, after Spain itself had been occupied by Napoleon, Delgado and his nephew Manuel José Arce led a rising against Spanish officials. It was put down, but it began the movement for independence.

After Central America broke from Spain in 1821, Delgado led San Salvador's resistance to joining the Mexican Empire. He then served in the Federal Republic of Central America, with leaders such as Morazán. He is a national hero of El Salvador.
